newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom says plans Eurobond in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom says plans Eurobond in 1997.

text.p: Russian natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom said in a statement on Tuesday it planned to issue Eurobonds in 1997 to help finance export projects.
It gave no details of volume, currency or timetable for the planned bonds.

"Taking into account the need to attract significant resources to finance the Yamal-Europe project and the favourable conditions for Russian companies to enter international financial markets, the board of directors on December 21 resolved to raise loans through issuing Eurobonds," the statement said.
Gazprom's main long-term capital expense is its $40 billion Yamal-Europe scheme to increase Russian natural gas production and exports to Europe.
A pipeline from the Yamal peninsula in western Siberia, capable of carrying 67 billion cubic metres of gas a year across 4,200 km to Germany, is expected to be operational by 2010.
Russia issued its first sovereign Eurobond since before the 1917 Bolshevik revolution in November and several cities and companies have expressed an interest in following suit.
